title: Church and the Poor
definition: Church and the Poor teaches the Church's responsibility to show mercy, generosity, justice, and practical concern for those in need.
summary: Church and the Poor addresses the congregation's responsibility to show mercy, justice, and practical care toward those in need.
christFocus: Jesus Christ identified with the lowly and calls His people to serve the least with love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The doctrine of the church and the poor teaches that God's people must not ignore those in material need. Scripture repeatedly connects true worship with justice, generosity, mercy, and concern for the poor.

This does not turn the church into merely a social agency. It shows that Gospel-shaped people cannot be indifferent to hunger, need, exploitation, or lack among neighbors and members.

Jesus became poor for our sake and showed compassion to the needy. The church honors Him when mercy is practiced without pride and truth is spoken without neglecting practical care.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because poverty can be treated either as invisible or as a political talking point. Scripture makes it personal: poor people bear God's image and must not be pushed to the edge of church concern.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice generosity with wisdom. Look for real needs in the congregation and community, avoid shaming people for poverty, and serve in ways that preserve dignity while pointing to Christ.
